meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Ms. Hale, or Mr., I haven't been told which. I have until 4:40, so I'll be brief. My son found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of your class. Withdraw it, and tell me who decided that.
Thank you for coming in. That's not an answer, Hale. Who decided to enter the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before they did?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
Students do a lot of things, Hale. We're here about one student, and you still haven't answered my question. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
You're leading me. I've done this for twenty years, and I know where "stressed" and "so it's possible" end up. Show me a document, or tell me why I shouldn't be upstairs with the principal.
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I don't answer hypotheticals about my son. "Possible" is not a basis for a zero, and it's not in your policy either. Is there a document, Hale, or not?
That's not what I said, and I'm writing down that you tried that. Ten minutes ago I asked you who decided and whether Owen was heard first. I'm still waiting.
